title: Embedding/Rerank Telemetry: Route-level dashboards, tracing, and cost attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: product and SRE teams lack fine-grained telemetry for the embeddings and reranking endpoints. Current dashboards only show global ingestion/latency for the model tier which obscures route-level regressions, batching behavior, and cost anomalies. This makes it slow to detect quality or performance regressions after changes (new model variants, batching config changes, or quantization profiles).

Proposal summary: build a route-aware observability surface for embeddings + rerank that includes: route-tagged Prometheus metrics, standard tracing spans for request lifecycle (router->matcher->embed->rerank), per-route Grafana dashboards with cost breakdown (tokens, GPU-seconds, batch benefits), and alerting rules for latency, error rate, and cost per 1k requests. Add lightweight sampling and synthetic traffic to prevent high cardinality explosion.

Goals:
- Provide a first-class Grafana dashboard template for any customer route within 2 clicks.
- Instrument the service code to emit stable labels: route_id, model_id, customer_tier, batch_size, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit.
- Surface tracing that allows correlating a single request (x-request-id) across router, runtime, and reranker worker with span durations for each stage.
- Provide cost attribution panels that estimate per-route cost using tokens * model-cost-coeff + GPU-seconds.
- Add alerting rules and runbook for noise-minimized, actionable signals.

Non-goals: full billing accuracy at first launch (we will provide estimates with documented error bounds), per-customer detailed billing exports (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Route-level Grafana dashboard template available in console with panels for P50/P95/P99 latency, requests per second, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, error rate, and estimated cost per 1k requests.
Tracing: a single x-request-id consistently ties together router -> runtime -> rerank spans; traces show per-stage durations and batch boundaries in >90% sampled test requests.
Metrics: Prometheus metrics emitted with stable label set (route_id, model_id, batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit) without unbounded cardinality growth in production sampling.
Alerting: at least three alert rules committed (route_latency_high, cost_spike, rerank_error_rate) with defined thresholds and linked runbook steps in PagerDuty playbook.
Load-tested: dashboards and metrics validated on a synthetic workload (mixed routes) at 5x typical production QPS with <15% overhead on p99 latency.
Docs: design doc + rollout checklist published in Confluence and linked in the ticket.
tasks: Design metric label schema and cardinality limits (Eng + Observability)
Add route_id and model metadata to existing metrics (router and runtime)
Implement tracing spans and context propagation (router, runtime, reranker worker)
Create Grafana dashboard template and embed in Console with route selector
Add Prometheus alert rules and PagerDuty runbook entries
Add cost-estimation helper (tokens -> estimated cost) and dashboard panels
E2E test with synthetic traffic and measure overhead
Ship docs: rollout plan, troubleshooting, and FAQ
dependencies: ENG-7104 (tracing infra upgrade to jaeger v2)
comments: 2025-02-16 Marco Chen: Scoped initial metric label set. Proposed labels: route_id, model_id, customer_tier, batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit, tokens_in_bucket. Added to tasks.
2025-02-18 Riley Thompson (SRE): Concern about cardinality from freeform route names. Recommendation: use stable route_id integer and a separate metadata endpoint for human-readable names.

2025-02-21 Design review: Agreed to limit high-card labels to batch_size_bucket and tokens_in_bucket to keep Prometheus cardinality bounded. Console will query metadata service for names when rendering dashboards.

2025-02-24 Aisha Patel: Implemented tracing PR draft for context headers (x-rw-request-id). Posting PR for review: runtime#1248. Need review from infra and security for header propagation in private deployments.

2025-02-27 Marco Chen: Ran synthetic test at 5x prod; metrics emitted successfully, but p99 latency increased by ~8% due to tracing sampling overhead. Decided to reduce default tracing sample rate to 1% for global, 10% for canary routes.

2025-03-01 SRE feedback: Alert thresholds tuned; route_latency_high set to P95>150ms sustained for 2 minutes for embeddings, P95>350ms for rerank. Cost_spike anchored to 30% increase over rolling 3h baseline.
2025-03-02 Marco Chen: Dashboard template merged; console embedding in review. Next: finalize runbook and schedule canary rollout next week.
